 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.45,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 22-09-2023 at about 9.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-AQ-6725 carefully, cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, on the left side of the road, at Dubbiganipalle Cross,
Madanapalle-Tirupathi main road, Kothavaripalle, Madanapalle Mandal, Andhra Pradesh.

At that time, a Pulsar motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-04-AJ-5130, Chassis No.MD2A11CZ9P-CE35363, ridden by its rider with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Madanapalle, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as mason (Supervisor) and was earning a sum of Rs.45,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Madanapalle Rural Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle, for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Sunakanti Venkatappa vs Jaripatti Naveen Kumar on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177523816/
2 vehicle.

sentences.text: Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.45,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to file his written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the existence of the policy in respect of the vehicle bearing No.AP-04-AJ-5130 of the respondent No.1.

It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained,
medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same without having driving licence at the material time of accident, which is in contravention of the policy conditions and also Motor Vehicles Act, the respondent No.1/owner of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.AP-04-AJ-5130 has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having the driving licence to ride the said motorcycle.

Further it is contended that, there is no fitness certificate and permit to the vehicle of the respondent No.1 to ply the said vehicle on the road at the material time of the accident and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
As such, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation or to indemnify the respondent No.1 in any manner whatsoever and the petition is liable to be dismissed against the respondent No.2.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner did not wear the helmet while driving the vehicle at the time of accident.
This is clear violation of provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act and its rules and also violation of the policy condition.
Further it is contended that, there is an inordinate delay in lodging the complaint and the time gap is completely utilized by the petitioner for concocting and creating false documents.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner was negligently riding his motorcycle in a zig-zag manner in the middle of the road, at the time of accident and came infront of the vehicle of the respondent No.1 and contributed to the accident.
The entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner.

But while lodging the complaint, the entire facts are twisted and lodged a false complaint and in collusion with the concerned police has managed to file the charge- sheet against the respondent No.1.
Further it is contended that, the alleged accident took place due to the negligence of the petitioner/ rider of motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-AQ- 6725.
Hence.
the liability if any, is to be saddled on the part of the owner and insurer of said motorcycle.
The owner and insurer of said vehicle are necessary party to the present case.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed for non- joinder of the necessary party.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismiss the petition.
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, from opposite direction.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his both legs, right hand and left side of his forehead.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.AP-40-AJ- 5130.
12.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.
But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident.

Further, the respondent No.2 has taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner and he was solely responsible for the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP- 40-AJ-5130.

It is contended that, at the time of accident the petitioner was negligently riding his motorcycle in a zig-zag manner in the middle of the road and came infront of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130 and contributed to the accident.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police has lodged a false complaint against the rider of insured motorcycle, to get compensation from the respondent No.2.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.2, who is the representative/Manager Legal of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-AJ-5130 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, from opposite direction and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his both legs, right hand and left side of his forehead and other parts of the body in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Further, the Ex.P.4 spot sketch clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on Madnapalle-Tirupathi main road, at Dubbiganipalle Cross, Kothavaripalle, Madanapalle Mandal,
Andhra Pradesh, in between the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130 and the motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-AQ-6725 of the petitioner, which were proceeding on the opposite direction.
Further, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further,
the investigation officer in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40- AJ-5130 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary,
Ex.P.12 radiological, x-ray and MRI reports (total 11), Ex.P.13 x-ray films (total 6), Ex.P.16 OPD card and Ex.P.17 x-ray
, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained left midshaft femur fracture, right distal tibia fracture and right 1st metacarpal fracture.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.

On the other hand,
there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 22-09-2023 at about 9:00 p.m., on Madnapalle-Tirupathi main road, at Dubbiganipalle Cross, Kothavaripalle, Madanapalle Mandal, Andhra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ- 5130.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained left midshaft femur fracture, right distal tibia fracture and right 1st metacarpal fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the year of birth of the petitioner is 1975.
The accident has taken place on 22-09- 2023 at about 9:00 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 48 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered left midshaft femur fracture, right distal tibia fracture and right 1st metacarpal fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 60% physical disability of both lower limbs and 30% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary, Ex.P.12 radiological, x-ray and MRI reports (total 11),
Ex.P.13 x-ray films (total 6), Ex.P.16 OPD card and Ex.P.17 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.

Though,
the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 22-09-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 05-10- 2024, which is after lapse of one year from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment to the petitioner.

As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Sunakanti Venkatappa vs Jaripatti Naveen Kumar on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177523816/
7 Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the petitioner has undergone surgery with respect to fracture of left femur and fracture of right tibia, the said fractures are united, implants are in situ.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as mason/supervisor and was earning more than Rs.45,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.

But, he has not produced any document to show that,
before accident he was working as mason/supervisor and was earning more than Rs.45,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,92,000/-.

b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 48 years is 13.

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,92,000 X 20/100 X 13 = Rs.4,99,200/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.7,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 33 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.6,36,972/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,36,972/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. left midshaft femur fracture, right distal tibia fracture and right 1 st metacarpal fracture.
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days from 23-09-2023 to 29-09-2023, in Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days in Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 7 = Rs.7,000/-

sentences.text: v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days in Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 7 =
Rs.5,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Ramagondanahalli, Whitefield, Varthur main road, Bengaluru, the accident has occurred on Madnapalle- Tirupathi main road, at Dubbiganipalle Cross, Kothavaripalle, Madanapalle Mandal, Andhra Pradesh and he has taken treatment at Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days as in-patient at Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.16,000 x 2 =
Rs.32,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 48 years and unfortunately he has suffered left midshaft femur fracture, right distal tibia fracture and right 1st metacarpal fracture.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body.

Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.50,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,30,772/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ- 5130.

As per Ex.R.4 insurance policy, the policy bearing No.417053/31/24/005197 issued by the respondent No.2 in respect offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ- 5130 was valid from 09-09-2023 to 08-09-2024.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
21.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the said charge-sheet has not been challenged by the respondent No.1 and even he did not care to appear in this case and establish that, as on the date of accident he was holding driving licence to ride the offending motorcycle.

Further, the Ex.R.2 driving licence extract of the respondent no.1 issued by ARTO Office, Madanapalli, clearly speaks that, the respondent No.1 was not holding driving licence to drive the motorcycle with gear, as on the date of accident.
He has applied and obtained the driving licence after the date of accident i.e. on 04-09-2025.
The same is deposed by the R.W.1, who is none other than the Junior Assistant, RTO Office, Madanapalli.
There is no contrary evidence on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2, with respect to same.

Therefore, in such circumstances, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.1 has committed breach of fundamental conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ- 5130.
As such, the respondent No.1 cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Accordingly, it is held that, the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, for the liability or compensation to be awarded to the petitioner.

Further, as the accident in question has taken place after the date of coming into force of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner that, even if there is breach of fundamental terms and conditions recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act, the insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the third party and recover the same from the insured, does not hold good.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, as there is breach of fundamental conditions of the Ex.R.4 insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1, in respect to offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AJ-5130, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization.
